# The question

The same question as the hard report asks, with soft topics: which topics
does the judge-steered Markov walk put into the seventeen lost verses of
P.Oxy. 5292 (vv. 13–29), and does that differ from what Sophocles writes
elsewhere? Here a lemma belongs to every topic with some probability, so the
posterior over a document's topic profile has no closed form and is
amortized by a neural network. The sections follow the hard report one by
one, so that the two can be read side by side.

# The model

A document is one whole restoration of the seventeen lost verses: its $N$
content lemmata, however many there are, drawn from the mixture
$\sum_k \theta_k \phi_k$ with $\theta \sim \mathrm{Dirichlet}(\mathbf 1)$.
The topic-word distributions $\phi$ ($K \times V$) are **soft**: a lemma has
probability under several topics, so every word is a mixture and the posterior
$p(\theta \mid \text{document})$ has no closed form. $\phi$ is fitted once on
Aeschylus and Euripides by a seeded latent Dirichlet allocation (tomotopy),
so that Sophocles, the baseline, is a test corpus like the restorations and
$\phi$ is not fitted on the text it is then compared with; each
of the unsupervised clusters of the hard model seeding one topic with
a strong word prior on all its lemmata, plus a few free topics.

The documents are those of the hard report: the walk, one document per
untilted snapshot, and Sophocles' extant trimeters in windows of seventeen,
the baseline. The walk is read on two levels: its **mean profile**, the
documents' posteriors averaged draw by draw, compared with Sophocles' by
$P(\bar\theta_k^{\text{walk}} > \bar\theta_k^{\text{Soph}})$ and the lift
of the means, and a **random document** against a random window,
$P(\theta_k^{\text{doc}} > \theta_k^{\text{window}})$. A topic is raised when
the mean-profile probability is at least 0.9 and the lift at least 1.5.

**Amortization.** A word enters the likelihood only through its $K$
log-likelihoods $\log \phi_{\cdot w}$, so a document is a set of $K$-vectors
and a DeepSet summary network is the natural compression. Documents differ
in length, so the set is padded and the network pools over the real elements
only, with $\log N$ as an extra summary. A coupling flow (BayesFlow) learns
$\theta$ in additive log-ratio coordinates from 200,000 simulated documents
whose lengths are drawn from the real documents' lengths. Before it reads
the real documents it is checked on 1000 held-out simulations: recovery
$R^2$, 90 % interval coverage, and simulation-based calibration (SBC), whose
rank histograms must be uniform if the posterior is calibrated.

# Data

The GPU work is done by `scripts/soft_model.py` (`slurm/soft_model.slurm`),
which reads the same dataset as the hard report
(`Urdatorn/bsda-miniproject-2026`: the bags of content lemmata, the
vocabulary with its cluster labels, the corpus of the three tragedians) and
writes to `results/soft/` the topic-word matrix with its top lemmata
(`phi.json`, and the whole matrix `phi_matrix.csv.gz`), the mean profiles
of the walk and of Sophocles with the walk's lift (`profiles.csv`), the
comparisons with the further baselines (`comparisons.csv`), the
calibration checks (`checks.csv`, `sbc.csv`, `recovery.csv`) and forty
documents with their amortized posterior for the check against NUTS below
(`exact_documents.json`). The trained network itself (`soft_flow.keras`) is
kept on the dataset, not in the repository. This document reads that
output.

```{r load, include = FALSE}
phi <- fromJSON(file.path(results_dir, "phi.json"))
profiles <- read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "profiles.csv"),
                     encoding = "UTF-8")
checks <- read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "checks.csv"), encoding = "UTF-8")
sbc <- read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "sbc.csv"), encoding = "UTF-8")
recovery <- read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "recovery.csv"),
                     encoding = "UTF-8")

topic_names <- phi$names
K <- length(topic_names)                          # seeded + free topics
H <- sum(profiles$source == "sophocles")          # seeded topics only
profiles$source <- factor(profiles$source, levels = c("sophocles", "walk"))
walk <- filter(profiles, source == "walk")

# The parts of the output a run writes last; the sections that need them
# are skipped, with a note, until it has
have_comparisons <- file.exists(file.path(results_dir, "comparisons.csv"))
have_exact <- file.exists(file.path(results_dir, "exact_documents.json")) &&
  file.exists(file.path(results_dir, "phi_matrix.csv.gz"))
figure <- function(paths) {
  drawn <- paths[file.exists(paths)]
  if (length(drawn) == 0) {
    cat("(figure not drawn yet:", paste(paths, collapse = ", "), ")")
  } else {
    knitr::include_graphics(drawn)
  }
}
```

`r H` seeded topics and `r K - H` free topics on a vocabulary of
`r phi$vocab_size` lemmata; the LDA's log-likelihood per word is
`r round(phi$ll_per_word, 3)`.

# The topics

The ten top lemmata of every topic as the seeded LDA fitted them on
Aeschylus and Euripides, with the number of seed lemmata found in the
vocabulary.

```{r topics, results = "asis"}
for (k in seq_len(K)) {
  topic <- topic_names[k]
  top_words <- paste(head(phi$top_words[[topic]], 10), collapse = " ")
  if (k <= H) {
    n_seeds <- length(phi$seeds_found[[topic]])
    cat("- **", topic, "** (", n_seeds, " seeds): ", top_words, "\n",
        sep = "")
  } else {
    cat("- **", topic, "** (free): ", top_words, "\n", sep = "")
  }
}
```

The vocabulary on the hard model's map, every lemma coloured instead by the
topic that gives it most probability under $\phi$ (`scripts/lemma_map.py`).
This is what soft topics buy: a word can belong elsewhere than its cluster
put it.

```{r soft_lemma_map, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%"}
figure("figures/soft_lemma_map.png")
```

# The posterior

The amortized posterior is a network, so before it reads a real document it
is checked on 1000 held-out simulated documents: how well the posterior
mean recovers the true $\theta$ ($R^2$ per topic), whether the 90 %
interval covers the truth 90 % of the time, and whether the ranks of the
truth among the posterior draws are uniform (simulation-based calibration,
with a Kolmogorov–Smirnov $p$-value per topic).


```{r checks}
knitr::kable(checks, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r sbc, fig.height = 6}
shown <- head(topic_names, params$show_topics)
sbc_shown <- filter(sbc, topic %in% shown)
sbc_shown$topic <- factor(sbc_shown$topic, levels = shown)
ggplot(sbc_shown, aes(x = bin, y = count)) +
  geom_col(fill = "grey60", width = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~ topic, ncol = 4) +
  labs(title = "SBC rank histograms (uniform if calibrated)",
       x = "rank of the true theta among the posterior draws, twenty bins",
       y = NULL)
```

```{r recovery, fig.height = 6}
recovery_shown <- filter(recovery, topic %in% shown)
recovery_shown$topic <- factor(recovery_shown$topic, levels = shown)
ggplot(recovery_shown, aes(x = true, y = post_mean)) +
  geom_abline(colour = "grey50") +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), colour = "grey80") +
  geom_point(size = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ topic, ncol = 4) +
  labs(title = "Recovery on held-out simulations (mean and 90 % interval)",
       x = "true theta", y = "posterior")
```

## Against the exact posterior

The checks above are on simulated documents, and the flow's training loss
was still falling when its schedule ended, so a calibrated posterior could
still be a needlessly wide one. The decisive check is on real documents:
with $\phi$ fixed, the posterior of one document is the low-dimensional
density

$$p(\theta \mid w_{1:N}) \propto \prod_{n=1}^{N} \sum_{k=1}^{K}
  \theta_k\, \phi_{k w_n}, \qquad \theta \sim \mathrm{Dirichlet}(\mathbf 1),$$

which NUTS samples exactly in a few seconds. Twenty snapshots of the walk
and twenty windows of Sophocles, drawn at random by the GPU script, are
sampled here with `rstan`, and their exact posterior is set beside the
flow's for every topic: the difference of the means, the ratio of the
standard deviations, and whether the flow's 90 % interval contains the
exact mean. (The chunks of this section run once
`exact_documents.json` and `phi_matrix.csv.gz` are in the results.)

```{r stan_model, eval = have_exact}
# The model: K topics, a document of N lemmata, the log of phi for each
# lemma of the document (row n is the lemma's log probability under every
# topic). The Dirichlet(1) prior is flat on the simplex, so only the
# likelihood is added.
stan_code <- "
data {
  int<lower=1> K;
  int<lower=1> N;
  matrix[N, K] log_phi;
}
parameters {
  simplex[K] theta;
}
model {
  vector[K] log_theta = log(theta);
  for (n in 1:N) {
    target += log_sum_exp(log_theta + log_phi[n]');
  }
}
"
exact_model <- stan_model(model_code = stan_code)
```

```{r exact, eval = have_exact, cache = TRUE}
phi_matrix <- read.csv(gzfile(file.path(results_dir, "phi_matrix.csv.gz")),
                       row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE,
                       encoding = "UTF-8")
phi_matrix <- as.matrix(phi_matrix)                  # K topics by V lemmata
exact_set <- fromJSON(file.path(results_dir, "exact_documents.json"),
                      simplifyVector = FALSE)
documents <- head(exact_set$documents, params$exact_docs)

# One row per document and topic: the flow's summary and the exact one
exact <- NULL
for (d in seq_along(documents)) {
  document <- documents[[d]]
  lemmata <- unlist(document$lemma_idx) + 1          # R counts from 1
  stan_data <- list(K = K, N = length(lemmata),
                    log_phi = t(log(phi_matrix[, lemmata])))
  fit <- sampling(exact_model, data = stan_data, chains = 4,
                  iter = params$exact_iter, warmup = 500, refresh = 0,
                  seed = 917)
  theta <- extract(fit, "theta")$theta               # draws by K
  rhat <- max(summary(fit)$summary[, "Rhat"], na.rm = TRUE)
  exact <- rbind(exact, data.frame(
    document = d, source = document$source, n_lemmata = length(lemmata),
    topic = topic_names,
    flow_mean = unlist(document$flow_mean), flow_sd = unlist(document$flow_sd),
    flow_q05 = unlist(document$flow_q05), flow_q95 = unlist(document$flow_q95),
    exact_mean = colMeans(theta), exact_sd = apply(theta, 2, sd),
    exact_q05 = apply(theta, 2, quantile, probs = 0.05),
    exact_q95 = apply(theta, 2, quantile, probs = 0.95),
    rhat = rhat))
}
exact$covered <- exact$flow_q05 <= exact$exact_mean &
  exact$exact_mean <= exact$flow_q95
exact$sd_ratio <- exact$flow_sd / exact$exact_sd
exact$z <- (exact$flow_mean - exact$exact_mean) / exact$exact_sd
```

Per set of documents: the mean absolute difference of the posterior means in
units of the exact posterior's standard deviation, the mean ratio of the
flow's standard deviation to the exact one (1 is right, above 1 is a flow
that hedges), the share of exact means inside the flow's 90 % interval
(0.9 if the flow is exact), and the largest $\hat R$ of any NUTS fit.

```{r exact_table, eval = have_exact}
exact_summary <- exact %>%
  group_by(source) %>%
  summarise(documents = n_distinct(document),
            mean_abs_z = mean(abs(z)),
            sd_ratio = mean(sd_ratio),
            covered = mean(covered),
            max_rhat = max(rhat))
knitr::kable(exact_summary, digits = 3)
```

```{r exact_plot, eval = have_exact, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(exact, aes(x = exact_mean, y = flow_mean)) +
  geom_abline(colour = "grey50") +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = flow_q05, ymax = flow_q95), colour = "grey80") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = exact_q05, xmax = exact_q95), height = 0,
                 colour = "grey80") +
  geom_point(size = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ source) +
  labs(title = "Amortized against exact posterior, every topic and document",
       x = "exact posterior mean (NUTS), with its 90 % interval",
       y = "amortized posterior mean, with its 90 % interval")
```

The topics where the two disagree most, by the absolute difference of
means in units of the exact standard deviation:

```{r exact_worst, eval = have_exact}
worst <- head(arrange(exact, desc(abs(z))), 8)
worst <- worst[, c("document", "source", "n_lemmata", "topic", "exact_mean",
                   "flow_mean", "exact_sd", "flow_sd", "z")]
knitr::kable(worst, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```


The two sets of documents.

```{r sizes}
sizes <- unique(profiles[, c("source", "n_docs", "n_lemmata")])
knitr::kable(sizes, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Documents, and content lemmata per document")
```

# Sophocles' baseline

```{r baseline, fig.height = 5}
sophocles_rows <- filter(profiles, source == "sophocles")
baseline_table <- data.frame(topic = factor(sophocles_rows$topic,
                                            rev(topic_names[1:H])),
                             mean = sophocles_rows$mean)
ggplot(baseline_table, aes(x = topic, y = mean)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "posterior mean of theta",
       title = paste("Sophocles,", sophocles_rows$n_docs[1],
                     "windows of seventeen trimeters"))
```

# Topics raised above Sophocles

Seeded topics whose mean profile is above Sophocles' with $P \ge 0.9$ and a
lift of at least 1.5, with the lift, the posterior mean and, in brackets,
the document-level probability.

```{r raised, results = "asis"}
walk$raised <- walk$p_above_sophocles >= 0.9 & walk$lift >= 1.5
raised <- arrange(filter(walk, raised), desc(lift))
if (nrow(raised) == 0) {
  cat("None.\n")
} else {
  items <- sprintf("%s (%.1f×, %.2f [%.2f])", raised$topic, raised$lift,
                   raised$mean, raised$p_document)
  cat(paste(items, collapse = ", "), "\n")
}
```

# Lift of every topic

```{r lifts, fig.height = 5}
lifts <- walk
lifts$topic <- factor(lifts$topic, levels = rev(topic_names[1:H]))
ggplot(lifts, aes(x = topic, y = lift, fill = raised)) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("grey70", "firebrick"),
                    name = "raised: P >= 0.9\nand lift >= 1.5") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "lift of the mean profile against Sophocles") +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# The largest lifts

The five topics with the largest lift.

```{r top}
top_five <- head(arrange(walk, desc(lift)), 5)
top_five <- top_five[, c("topic", "mean", "q05", "q95", "p_above_sophocles",
                         "lift", "p_document")]
knitr::kable(top_five, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE)
```

# Beyond Sophocles: three baselines

The same two further baselines as in the hard report, Aeschylus and
Euripides and Classical Attic (`data/attic_windows.parquet`, windows of 28
lemmata of the Attic authors before Alexander), read here through the
amortized posterior: every baseline window is a document, the baseline's
mean profile is compared with the walk's draw by draw, and a lift's 90 %
interval is that of the ratio of the two mean profiles over the posterior
draws, not a bootstrap. `scripts/soft_circles.py` draws the grids from
`results/soft/comparisons.csv`.

```{r soft_circles_walk, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%"}
figure(c("figures/soft_circles_walk_vs_sophocles.png",
         "figures/soft_circles_walk_vs_tragedians.png",
         "figures/soft_circles_walk_vs_attic.png"))
```

Sophocles as the focus, against the other two tragedians and against
Classical Attic:

```{r soft_circles_sophocles, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%"}
figure(c("figures/soft_circles_sophocles_vs_tragedians.png",
         "figures/soft_circles_sophocles_vs_attic.png"))
```

```{r soft_baselines_table, eval = have_comparisons}
comparisons <- read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "comparisons.csv"),
                        encoding = "UTF-8")
comparisons$off_one <- comparisons$lift_q05 > 1 | comparisons$lift_q95 < 1
baseline_rows <- NULL
for (comparison in unique(comparisons$comparison)) {
  these <- filter(comparisons, comparison == !!comparison, off_one)
  these <- arrange(these, desc(lift))
  largest <- paste(sprintf("%s %.2f", head(these$topic, 3),
                           head(these$lift, 3)), collapse = ", ")
  smallest <- paste(sprintf("%s %.2f", tail(these$topic, 3),
                            tail(these$lift, 3)), collapse = ", ")
  baseline_rows <- rbind(baseline_rows,
                         data.frame(comparison = comparison,
                                    off_one = nrow(these),
                                    largest = largest, smallest = smallest))
}
knitr::kable(baseline_rows, row.names = FALSE,
             col.names = c("comparison", "topics off 1", "largest lifts",
                           "smallest lifts"))
```

The topic the hard report singles out, *wrong-vengeance-err*, under the
soft model:

```{r soft_wrong_vengeance, eval = have_comparisons}
one_topic <- filter(comparisons, topic == "wrong-vengeance-err")
one_topic <- one_topic[, c("comparison", "lift", "lift_q05", "lift_q95",
                           "p_document")]
knitr::kable(one_topic, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

# Which seeded topic dominates

A reading the soft model alone affords, since its posterior is over the
whole simplex at once: for a random document of the walk or of Sophocles,
the probability that each seeded topic is the largest.

```{r dominant, fig.height = 7}
heat <- profiles
heat$topic <- factor(heat$topic, levels = rev(topic_names[1:H]))
ggplot(heat, aes(x = source, y = topic, fill = p_dominant)) +
  geom_tile() +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "firebrick",
                      name = "P(largest\nseeded topic)") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
       title = "Which seeded topic dominates a random document")
```

The five largest mean profiles of Sophocles and of the walk.

```{r mass}
columns <- c("source", "topic", "mean", "q05", "q95", "lift",
             "p_above_sophocles", "p_document")
top_five <- rbind(head(arrange(sophocles_rows, desc(mean)), 5)[, columns],
                  head(arrange(walk, desc(mean)), 5)[, columns])
knitr::kable(top_five, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```
